identity.name: Tanzania
alt_names: United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar

land.text: Tanganyika, the British-administered Tanganyika Territory, held 'under a League of Nations mandate in 1922'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's British Africa shape of 1960 (3.6 M km2) still holds mainland Tanganyika; its British East Africa row (1961..1968) holds Zanzibar, which joined in 1964 (see the ledger), and not the mainland.

capitals.name: Dar es Salaam
capitals.note: Infobox: largest city 06°48′S 39°16′E, 'the former capital'. The Dodoma page: in 1974 the government announced the capital would move from Dar es Salaam; it 'became the official capital in 1996'; Dar es Salaam remains 'the commercial and de facto capital'.

capitals.name: Dodoma
capitals.note: Official capital from 1996 (Dodoma page); the President's office and the ministries 'completed the move to the city's Mtumba area in 2019'.

keyframe_review.note: 882,652 km2 for Tanganyika alone, 1961-62; the infobox gives 944,842 km2 (no year), ratio 0.93, so the shape is within the honest precision (the page does not say whether the figure includes inland water). The page records no boundary change beyond the 1964 union. Cliopatria starts in 1961 and the state is independent from 9 December 1961.

correction.text: Tanganyika alone, unchanged, for 1963 only; from 26 April 1964 the United Republic also holds Zanzibar (see tanzania_1964)

keyframe_review.note: Only the years change: Cliopatria draws mainland Tanganyika alone through 1966 and adds Zanzibar in 1967, but the page dates the union to Union Day, 26 April 1964 (Articles of Union signed 22 April, Act of Union 25 April). Cliopatria's Sultanate of Zanzibar row (1963..1966) is therefore three years too long.

correction.text: Tanganyika joined with the People's Republic of Zanzibar to form the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar on 26 April 1964; renamed Tanzania on 29 October 1964

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1964-1966: mainland Tanganyika plus the Zanzibar archipelago (Cliopatria's 4,245 km2 Zanzibar shape). The sum, about 886,500 km2, equals Cliopatria's own 1967 shape (886,467 km2), so only the dating is wrong. The Zanzibar Revolution page gives 26 April for Karume's announcement but also 23 April for the merger; the Tanganyika and Tanzania pages both say 26 April.
886,467 km2, Tanganyika plus Zanzibar (+4,189 km2 on the 1963 shape); infobox 947,303 km2 (no year), ratio 0.94. Right for 1967-72 and correct from 1964, as the new keyframe says.

887,273 km2, 0.1% above 1967 and 0.1% above 1976: cartographic noise, no event on any page opened explains it. Infobox 947,303 km2 (ratio 0.94). The Kagera Salient dispute of 1978 is a contest zone in the ledger, not a change of this shape.

886,212 km2 to 2023; the page records no boundary dispute or change after 1964 (it does not mention Lake Nyasa). Tanzania lost nothing in the Uganda war (the Kagera Salient was retaken by January 1979) and held Ugandan soil in 1979 (occupation events).

region.text: Tanganyika, the former British-administered Tanganyika Territory

ledger.note: 1961-12-09: Tanganyika becomes independent. 'It first gained independence from the United Kingdom on 9 December 1961 as a Commonwealth realm'; before that it was the British-administered Tanganyika Territory ('under a League of Nations mandate in 1922'). Nyerere 'continued as prime minister when Tanganyika became independent in 1961' (Tanzania page).

1962-12-09: Tanganyika becomes a republic within the Commonwealth. The infobox lists 'Republic: 9 December 1962'; the Tanzania page adds 'a democratic republic under an executive president'. No change of territory.

region.text: the Zanzibar archipelago, the People's Republic of Zanzibar

ledger.note: 1964-04-26: Tanganyika and Zanzibar unite as the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar. The page says Tanganyika 'officially joined with the People's Republic of Zanzibar' on 'Union Day, 26 April 1964' (Articles of Union 22 April, Act of Union 25 April); the Tanzania page: 'the archipelago merged with mainland Tanganyika on 26 April 1964'. The Sultan had been overthrown on 12 January 1964 (Zanzibar Revolution page). Cliopatria adds the islands only in 1967.

1964-10-29: the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar is renamed Tanzania. 'On 29 October of the same year, the country was renamed the United Republic of Tanzania' ('Tan' from Tanganyika, 'Zan' from Zanzibar).

region.text: 'a 720 square miles (1,900 km2) stretch of land between the official border and the Kagera River' (the Kagera Salient)

ledger.note: 1978-10: Uganda invades the Kagera Salient. 'In October 1978, Ugandan forces began making incursions into Tanzania' and 'Later that month, the Uganda Army launched an invasion'; on 1 November Radio Uganda 'declared that the Kagera River marked the new border', and on 2 November Nyerere declared war.

region.text: 'a 720 square miles (1,900 km2) stretch of land between the official border and the Kagera River' (the Kagera Salient)

ledger.note: 1979-01: the Kagera Salient is retaken. 'On 23 November, three TPDF brigades crossed the pontoon bridge and began reoccupying the Kagera Salient'; 'By early January, all Ugandan troops had been ejected from Kagera'.

region.text: Uganda, which the Tanzanian army (TPDF) 'occupied ... facing only scattered resistance' until it 'secured the Uganda-Sudan border in June' 1979

ledger.note: 1979-04: Tanzanian forces hold Uganda after Kampala falls. 'On 10 April a combined TPDF-UNLF force attacked Kampala, and secured it the following day'; 'In the following months, the TPDF occupied Uganda'. The TPDF Southern Brigade had 'finally crossed the border on the night of 21 January and attacked Mutukula the following day'; January-April 1979 is the war's zone (wars) and the contest in Uganda's dossier. The page gives no map of the occupied ground, so the region is Uganda as a whole as it stood by June. (Reviewer af-08-i moved this from 1979-01 to 1979-04 to match the page and republic-of-uganda's occupation_start of April 1979.)

region.text: Uganda, which the Tanzanian army (TPDF) 'occupied ... facing only scattered resistance' until it 'secured the Uganda-Sudan border in June' 1979

ledger.note: 1979-06: the war ends. The TPDF 'secured the Uganda-Sudan border in June, bringing the war to an end' (infobox: 9 October 1978 - 3 June 1979, 'Tanzanian victory ... Idi Amin flees into exile'). The page gives no date for the Tanzanian withdrawal, so this end is the war's, bridging a silence; a gap-filler must date the real withdrawal from another page.

1996: Dodoma becomes the official capital. 'It became the official capital in 1996' (the government had announced the move from Dar es Salaam in 1974); the President's office completed the move to Mtumba in 2019.

wars.name: Zanzibar Revolution
wars.outcome: The revolution 'began on 12 January 1964 and led to the overthrow of the Sultan of Zanzibar'; the country was renamed the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba, and on 26 April it united with Tanganyika.
wars.note: Tanganyika was not a belligerent; listed because the revolution created the union that is Tanzania's only territorial gain. The page does not state a date for the new republic's proclamation.

wars.name: Uganda-Tanzania War

zones.text: 'a 720 square miles (1,900 km2) stretch of land between the official border and the Kagera River' (the Kagera Salient)
Uganda, which the Tanzanian army (TPDF) 'occupied ... facing only scattered resistance' until it 'secured the Uganda-Sudan border in June' 1979

wars.outcome: Tanzanian victory (9 October 1978 - 3 June 1979): Uganda declared the annexation of the Kagera Salient (1 November 1978) and had been ejected from it by early January 1979; Tanzania then invaded and occupied Uganda, taking Kampala on 10-11 April, and Idi Amin was deposed.
wars.note: The page gives the Tanzanian crossing into Uganda as the night of 21 January 1979, the offensive in mid-February, Kampala 10-11 April and the Sudan border in June; it gives no date for the last Tanzanian troops leaving Uganda.

certainty.note: Inherited colonial frontiers of Tanganyika plus the archipelago of Zanzibar. The Tanzania page records no boundary dispute (it does not mention Lake Nyasa), so no frontier is marked soft; the Kagera Salient of 1978-79 is a war zone, not an uncertain line (the page gives its size, 1,900 km2, and the Kagera River as Uganda's claimed border).

notes: Tanzania: Cliopatria row 'Tanzania' 1961..2024 (six shapes), reviewed with five pages (budget: up to 5). (1) Cliopatria adds Zanzibar to the Tanzania shape only in 1967 and keeps a Sultanate of Zanzibar row to 1966; the pages date the union to 26 April 1964, so 1964-1966 gets a new keyframe (Tanganyika plus Zanzibar) and the Sultanate of Zanzibar row should end in 1964 in its own dossier (Zanzibar is a sultanate to the 12 January 1964 revolution, then the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba to the union). (2) Tanganyika's predecessor is the British Africa row (its 1960 shape holds the mainland); the British East Africa row (1961..1968) holds Zanzibar and The Gambia, not the mainland. (3) The Tanzanian withdrawal from Uganda is not dated on the Uganda-Tanzania War page: the occupation_end is set at the war's end (June 1979) at confidence 1 and needs a page. (4) The 'Kagera Salient' region name is not in the gazetteer; see gazetteer_names_needed. (5) The Tanzania page does not mention any boundary dispute with Malawi (Lake Nyasa) and the budget did not allow a further page. (6) Rulers omitted: no page opened gives a list of presidents (Nyerere is named as prime minister from 1961). (7) The 1973 and 1976 shapes differ from 1967 by about 0.1% with no cause on any page; treated as noise.
